introduction: Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd is a cotton yarn dyeing and knitted fabric finishing company supplying export brands. Its operations are carried out across three locations: Unit 1 Dyeing House at SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode, Tamil Nadu, where dyeing and finishing take place; Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse on the same campus, which houses the effluent treatment plant and the storage of chemicals and finished goods; and the Head Office on Avinashi Road, Coimbatore, which accommodates administration, human resources, procurement and information technology.

This Standard Operating Procedures manual, reference MTPL/SOP/01, consolidates the procedures through which the Environment, Health and Safety, Production, Quality, Human Resources, Procurement, Finance, Information Technology and Administration departments conduct their day-to-day work. It sets out the responsibilities of each department and role, the sequence of activities, the records to be maintained and the controls applied at each stage of the process.

This document is Revision 01. It replaces any earlier unnumbered procedures or informal working practices in the areas it covers, and it is intended to be read alongside site-specific work instructions, permits and records that reference it.
front.objective: To establish a consistent, documented and controlled framework of procedures across Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that every site and department performs its activities in a planned, repeatable and verifiable manner, with clear accountability for environmental, health and safety, quality, resource and compliance outcomes.
benefits: Provides a single, version-controlled reference for staff at Unit 1, Unit 2 and the Head Office, reducing variation in how the same task is performed between sites.
Clarifies roles and responsibilities between departments, so that handovers, approvals and escalations are traceable to a named function.
Supports consistent control of chemicals, effluent and waste handling at Unit 2 and Unit 1, reducing the likelihood of unplanned releases and non-conformities.
Gives buyers, auditors and internal reviewers a clear basis against which to verify that work is carried out as documented.
Enables new and transferred employees to be inducted and assessed against a defined standard, shortening the time needed to reach competence.
Creates a structured basis for continual improvement, as deviations and near misses recorded against these procedures can be analysed and the procedures revised accordingly.

coreValues.title: Safety First
coreValues.description: No task is so urgent that it may be performed without the controls set out for it, and every employee is empowered to stop work where a risk is not adequately controlled.

coreValues.title: Accountability
coreValues.description: Each procedure names the function responsible for carrying it out and for the records that evidence it, so that ownership of every outcome is clear.

coreValues.title: Environmental Stewardship
coreValues.description: Meridian manages water, effluent, chemicals and waste responsibly, treating environmental performance as an integral part of production rather than a separate activity.

coreValues.title: Transparency
coreValues.description: Deviations, incidents and non-conformities are recorded accurately and reported through the defined channels, without concealment, so that they can be investigated and learned from.

front.howToUse: Users should first identify the procedure relevant to their task from the contents list and read it in full before starting work, including its scope, referenced documents and records. Where a procedure refers to a site-specific work instruction or permit, that document must be consulted and followed alongside this manual. Printed copies are uncontrolled unless stamped with a controlled copy number; the current controlled version is held electronically by the Head Office and must be checked before use. Any suggested improvement or query should be raised with the responsible department head rather than acted upon informally.
front.reviewMechanism: This manual shall be reviewed at least annually, and additionally following any significant incident, audit finding, change in process or equipment, change in legal or customer requirement, or change in organisational responsibility. Each department head shall submit proposed amendments to the Quality function, which shall coordinate review with EHS and the relevant department, record the changes in the revision history, and issue the revised version under a new revision number with the superseded copies withdrawn from use. Review outcomes, including decisions not to change a procedure, shall be recorded and retained.
front.approvalStatement: This Standard Operating Procedures manual, MTPL/SOP/01 Revision 01, is approved for implementation across Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd with effect from the date of signature by the authorised management representative.

sops.title: Waste Segregation and Disposal
sops.purpose: To define how solid, hazardous and effluent-related wastes arising at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd are identified, segregated at source, stored, collected, documented and disposed of through authorised channels, so that environmental harm and statutory non-compliance are prevented and the company can evidence control of its waste streams.
sops.scope: Applies to all waste generated at Unit 1 Dyeing House (dyeing and finishing), Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse (ETP, chemical and finished goods storage), and Head Office, Avinashi Road, Coimbatore (administration, HR, procurement, IT), both during routine operations and during maintenance, shutdowns and chemical changeovers. It covers all personnel and contractors who handle, transport or dispose of waste on the SIPCOT Perundurai campus or on behalf of the company.

definitions.definition: Any material generated by company activities that is discarded, intended for discard, or no longer usable in its original purpose, including solid, liquid and sludge forms.
The separation of waste into defined categories at the point of generation, using labelled and colour-coded containers, before any mixing can occur.

Waste carrying chemical, physical or toxic properties that require special handling, including spent dye liquors, chemical containers, spent solvents and oily rags, as identified in the site hazardous waste inventory.
Residual solids separated from wastewater in the Effluent Treatment Plant, including chemical sludge from primary and secondary treatment.
The controlled log in which each consignment of waste leaving site is recorded with category, quantity, date, collector and receiving facility details.
A transporter or disposal facility approved by the EHS Manager and holding the permissions required for the relevant waste category, whose approval status is reviewed annually.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and maintains the site waste inventory and hazardous waste category list.
Approves Authorised Collectors and reviews their permissions annually.
Reviews the Waste Manifest Register and reports waste KPIs to management.
Ensures segregation bins are placed, labelled and used correctly at every dyeing and finishing station.
Reports spills, container damage and unlabelled waste to the EHS Manager the same shift.
Manages effluent sludge drying, storage and dispatch and records quantities generated.
Keeps the ETP waste storage area free of incompatible materials.
Notifies EHS before rejected or off-specification fabric and yarn lots are scrapped, so that textile waste can be routed correctly.
Ensures contracts with waste collectors and disposal facilities require valid permissions and provision of disposal certificates before onboarding.
Ensure office waste streams at Head Office are segregated and collected, and that new staff receive waste segregation induction.

procedure.heading: Waste identification and categorisation
procedure.body: The EHS Manager maintains the site waste inventory, listing each waste stream by source, physical form and category. Each category is assigned a colour-coded container and a storage location. The inventory is reviewed whenever a new process, chemical or product is introduced.
substeps: Record new waste streams before first generation.
Confirm hazardous status using chemical safety data sheets supplied by Procurement.

procedure.heading: Segregation at source
procedure.body: Production and ETP personnel place waste directly into the designated container for its category at the point of generation. Mixing of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, or of incompatible chemicals, is not permitted. Containers must carry a label showing waste category, source and date.
substeps: Keep lids closed when containers are not in use.
Do not overfill; containers are replaced when about three-quarters full.

procedure.heading: Interim storage
procedure.body: Segregated waste is moved to the designated storage area at Unit 2 or the relevant Unit 1 holding point at least once per shift. Hazardous waste is stored on impervious surfaces with secondary containment, away from drains and from finished goods. Storage areas are inspected weekly for leaks, labelling and housekeeping.
substeps: Segregate stored materials by compatibility.
Record weekly inspection results on the storage checklist.

procedure.heading: Effluent sludge handling
procedure.body: Effluent sludge from the ETP is dewatered, weighed and stored in lined, labelled bays pending collection. Quantities generated each month are recorded against the ETP log. Sludge is not released to any drain, open ground or unauthorised location.
substeps: Record weight at point of dispatch.
Check moisture and labelling before loading.

procedure.heading: Collection and dispatch
procedure.body: Waste is dispatched only to Authorised Collectors. Before loading, the EHS Manager or a delegated officer confirms the collector's current permissions and checks the consignment category against the inventory. Each dispatch is entered in the Waste Manifest Register before the vehicle leaves site.
substeps: Verify collector permission validity on the day of dispatch.
Sign the manifest on departure and retain the copy.

procedure.heading: Disposal documentation
procedure.body: Disposal certificates or receipts from the receiving facility are obtained for every consignment and filed against the corresponding Waste Manifest Register entry. Any consignment without a returned receipt within the agreed period is escalated to the EHS Manager for follow-up with the collector.
substeps: Chase outstanding receipts within five working days.

procedure.heading: Head Office waste
procedure.body: Office waste at Head Office, Avinashi Road, is segregated into dry recyclables, general waste and electronic waste. Electronic waste from IT is held in a secure area and disposed of only through an Authorised Collector, with the disposal recorded in the Waste Manifest Register.
substeps: Log all decommissioned IT equipment before removal from site.

procedure.heading: Incident and spill response
procedure.body: Any spill, leak or mis-disposal of waste is reported immediately to the EHS Manager and contained using the spill kit at the relevant location. The incident is recorded, root cause is established and corrective action is agreed and tracked to closure.
substeps: Isolate the area and prevent entry into drains.
Complete an incident report within 24 hours.

Head Office staff receive a briefing on office waste segregation during induction. Attendance is recorded by HR and the EHS Manager confirms competence through observation at the first site visit.

sops.title: Hazardous Chemical Storage and Handling
sops.purpose: To define the controls for receiving, storing, handling, dispensing, transporting within site and disposing of hazardous chemicals at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that risks to people, the environment and the ETP are minimised and the company can demonstrate compliance with its internal EHS requirements.
sops.scope: Applies to all hazardous chemicals, dye auxiliaries, process chemicals and wastes handled at Unit 1 Dyeing House and Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode, including chemical stores, dosing areas, laboratories, ETP chemical dosing and waste storage. It covers all employees, contractors and visitors who handle or are exposed to these chemicals. Head Office procurement activities that initiate chemical purchases are included only insofar as they affect receipt and storage at site.

definitions.definition: Any substance or preparation that is flammable, corrosive, toxic, oxidising, reactive or otherwise presents a risk to health, safety or the environment, as identified on its Safety Data Sheet (SDS).
The supplier-issued document describing the hazards, handling, storage, first-aid and emergency measures for a chemical, held current in the chemical register for each product.
The controlled, site-specific list of all hazardous chemicals held on site, showing quantity, location, SDS reference, compatibility group and responsible area.
A classification assigned to each chemical so that incompatible materials, such as acids and alkalis or oxidisers and organics, are segregated during storage and transport.
A secondary containment area, sized to hold the volume of the largest container in the stored group plus an allowance for rainfall, to contain leaks or spills.
A designated, ventilated and bunded location within the Dyeing House where chemicals are weighed, measured or transferred into process vessels.
A stocked set of absorbents, neutralisers, personal protective equipment and disposal bags positioned at each storage and dispensing location.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and maintains the chemical register and compatibility matrix.
Approves new chemicals before receipt and reviews SDS currency quarterly.
Audits storage areas, dispensing points and the ETP chemical store and tracks corrective actions.
Reports KPI performance to management review.
Ensures dyeing and finishing staff use only approved dispensing points and quantities.
Confirms that process chemical requirements are issued from the store against approved batch sheets.
Stops work where unsafe chemical handling is observed.
Verifies incoming chemical batch conformity and checks that certificates of analysis are filed with the chemical register entry.
Controls sampling and retention of chemical samples in the laboratory.
Places orders only for chemicals that have been cleared by EHS and that carry a current SDS.
Ensures suppliers deliver with labelled containers and SDS copies.
Receives, inspects and stores chemicals in designated compatible locations.
Maintains stock records, inspects containers and bunds weekly, and manages waste chemical storage.
Schedules chemical handling training and PPE issue, and keeps training records current.

procedure.heading: Approval of new chemicals
procedure.body: No hazardous chemical may be purchased or introduced to site until the EHS Manager has reviewed its SDS and assigned a compatibility group. The EHS Manager records the approval in the chemical register before the Procurement Officer raises the order.
substeps: Requesting department submits the product name, SDS and proposed quantity.
EHS Manager assigns hazard class, compatibility group and storage requirement.

procedure.heading: Receipt and inspection
procedure.body: On arrival at Unit 2, the Store Keeper checks each delivery against the purchase order and the SDS, and inspects containers for damage, leaks and correct labelling. Non-conforming or unlabelled containers are refused or quarantined and reported to EHS the same shift. Accepted goods are logged in the stock record before being moved to storage.
substeps: Confirm labels show product name, hazard pictograms and batch number.
Quarantine damaged containers in the designated quarantine bay.

procedure.heading: Segregated storage
procedure.body: Chemicals are stored by compatibility group in the labelled location shown on the chemical register, with acids, alkalis, oxidisers and flammables kept apart. Containers are kept closed, off the floor on pallets, and within bunded areas sized to contain the largest container in each group. Storage areas are kept clear of combustible waste and ignition sources.
substeps: Display the compatibility group sign at each bay entrance.
Keep aisle access and emergency exits unobstructed at all times.

procedure.heading: Dispensing and use in production
procedure.body: Chemicals are issued to Unit 1 only against an approved batch sheet, and are dispensed only at designated dispensing points using the required personal protective equipment. Operators confirm the chemical identity and quantity against the batch sheet before dispensing and return unused quantities and empty containers to the store. Spills at dispensing points are cleaned immediately using the spill kit and recorded.
substeps: Wear PPE as specified on the SDS and batch sheet before opening any container.
Use secondary containers that are labelled with contents and hazard information.

procedure.heading: Internal transport
procedure.body: Chemicals moved between Unit 2 and Unit 1 are carried in sealed, secured and labelled containers on approved trolleys or vehicles, and never carried in unmarked vessels. Transfers are logged with date, time, quantity and receiving person. Drivers and operators are trained in the spill response procedure before undertaking transfers.
substeps: Load only containers that are closed and in good condition.
Record each transfer on the movement log.

procedure.heading: Inspection and housekeeping
procedure.body: Storage areas, bunds, spill kits, labels and dispensing points are inspected weekly by the Store Keeper or ETP Supervisor, with monthly audits by the EHS Manager. Defects, leaks, missing labels and expired SDS are recorded and corrected within the timescale set on the action log. Overdue corrective actions are escalated to the EHS Manager.
procedure.responsible: Store Keeper and ETP Supervisor (Unit 2); EHS Manager
substeps: Check bund integrity and drain valves are closed where required.
Verify spill kit contents against the inventory list.

procedure.heading: Spill and emergency response
procedure.body: Any spill or leak is reported immediately to the nearest supervisor and EHS, and the area is isolated while the spill kit is used by trained staff. Spilt material and contaminated absorbents are placed in labelled waste containers and not washed into drains. Serious spills or exposures trigger the site emergency response plan, and an incident report is raised within 24 hours.
substeps: Consult the SDS first-aid and firefighting sections before responding.
Keep spilt material out of the ETP inlet unless ETP operations have approved it.

procedure.heading: Waste chemical storage and disposal
procedure.body: Waste chemicals and contaminated materials are stored in labelled, compatible and closed containers in the designated waste store, separated from usable stock. Disposal is only through authorised contractors, with each consignment supported by a waste transfer record reconciled against the waste register. The EHS Manager reviews waste records monthly.
substeps: Record waste type, quantity and date on the waste register before collection.
Retain signed transfer notes with the waste register.

Refresher training is given annually and after any significant incident or procedure change. The HR and Training Coordinator keeps attendance records and the EHS Manager verifies content.

sops.title: Energy Efficiency in Dyeing Operations
sops.purpose: To define how Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd plans, controls, measures and improves energy use in cotton yarn dyeing and knitted fabric finishing at Unit 1 Dyeing House, so that energy consumption per kilogram of processed fabric is reduced in a controlled and verifiable way without compromising shade, fastness or quality requirements.
sops.scope: This procedure applies to all dyeing, washing, drying, stentering and related finishing operations at Unit 1 Dyeing House, SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode, including steam, electricity, diesel and compressed air consumed by these operations. It covers batch and continuous process lines and the associated utilities. It does not cover effluent treatment energy at Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, which is managed under the ETP operating procedures, nor administrative energy use at the Head Office, Avinashi Road, Coimbatore.

definitions.definition: The total energy consumed by the dyeing and finishing operations in a defined period, divided by the good production output in kilograms for the same period, expressed as kWh or MJ per kg of fabric or yarn processed.

The reference value of SEC for a process route, product group or machine, established from at least one month of metered data under normal operating conditions and approved by the Production Head before any improvement is credited.

A recorded opportunity to reduce energy use, such as liquor ratio reduction, steam trap repair, heat recovery installation or batch loading optimisation, that has an assigned owner, target date and verified outcome.
The weight ratio of dye liquor or process water to textile material in a dyeing machine, which directly affects the heating and pumping energy required per batch.

A dyeing or finishing setting, such as temperature ramp rate, hold time, pH or stenter temperature, that must remain within the approved recipe window to ensure shade, fastness and dimensional quality, and that therefore may not be altered for energy saving without quality approval.
A recorded value from a sub-meter or utility meter for steam, electricity, diesel or compressed air, taken at a defined frequency and attributed to a specific machine or line.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and approves energy baselines and SEC targets for Unit 1 Dyeing House.
Approves energy audit actions and resourcing for their implementation.
Reviews monthly SEC performance and escalates deviations to the Unit management review.
Record batch-level energy data and machine loading information for every batch processed.
Ensure machines are run to approved liquor ratios and loading limits.
Report steam leaks, trap failures and abnormal consumption to the Production Head the same shift.
Approve any change to a Critical Process Parameter proposed for energy reduction.
Confirm that shade, fastness and dimensional results are unaffected before a new recipe is released.
Verify that boiler, steam and compressed air systems are operated and maintained safely during energy improvement works.
Include energy-related hazards in the Unit 1 risk assessments.
Maintain energy sub-meters, calibration records and the planned maintenance schedule for steam traps, insulation, pumps and motors.
Procure approved energy-saving spares and services through the Procurement department.

procedure.heading: Establish the energy baseline
procedure.body: For each dyeing machine, finishing line and utility system, the Dyeing Shift Supervisors shall collect metered energy and production data for a minimum of one calendar month under normal operating conditions. The Production Head shall review the data, exclude abnormal periods such as breakdowns, and approve the resulting SEC baseline for each process route.
substeps: Confirm sub-meter identification and calibration status before data collection starts.
Record the baseline in the Energy Baseline Register.

procedure.heading: Set SEC targets and improvement plan
procedure.body: The Production Head shall set an annual SEC reduction target for Unit 1 and break it down by process route. Each target shall be supported by a list of energy audit actions with owners, resources and target dates, reviewed against the approved baseline.

procedure.heading: Plan batches to reduce energy use
procedure.body: Production planning shall group batches of similar shade depth and temperature profile to minimise machine idle time and repeated heating or cooling cycles. Full-load batching shall be used wherever the approved recipe permits, and batches shall not exceed the machine's rated loading.
substeps: Use the approved liquor ratio for each recipe and do not increase water volume without a documented reason.
Schedule pre-heating of common utilities to coincide with batch start times.

procedure.heading: Control critical process parameters
procedure.body: Any proposal to change a Critical Process Parameter for energy saving shall be submitted in writing to the Quality Manager. Energy trials shall be run only after written approval, and the resulting shade, fastness and dimensional results shall be recorded before the new settings are released to routine production.

procedure.heading: Operate and monitor utilities
procedure.body: Dyeing Shift Supervisors shall record steam, electricity and compressed air readings at the frequency set in the Energy Monitoring Plan and log all batches against their energy data. Abnormal readings or consumption above the SEC baseline by a defined tolerance shall be investigated the same shift.
substeps: Check steam traps, insulation and condensate return during each shift walk-down.
Isolate idle machines and pumps where the process allows.

procedure.heading: Maintain energy equipment
procedure.body: The Maintenance Lead shall carry out planned maintenance of steam traps, boiler controls, pumps, motors, insulation and sub-meters. Defects found shall be repaired within the agreed timeframe, and the work shall be recorded against the equipment identification.

procedure.heading: Review performance and close actions
procedure.body: The Production Head shall review monthly SEC data against target and baseline at the Unit management review. Each energy audit action shall be closed only when the saving has been verified against the baseline, and any action not achieved shall be re-planned with a revised date.
substeps: Record verified savings in the Energy Audit Action log.
Share lessons learned with all dyeing shifts.

procedure.body: This SOP shall be reviewed at least annually, or earlier after a significant change in machines, fuels, recipes or regulatory requirements. Revisions shall be approved by the Production Head and issued under MTPL/SOP/01 document control.

sops.title: Water Conservation and Effluent Treatment
sops.purpose: To define how Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd conserves water across the Dyeing House and finishing operations at Unit 1 and how process effluent is collected, treated at the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) in Unit 2, monitored and discharged or reused in a controlled manner that keeps every discharge within the limits set in the applicable consent to operate and the company's internal limits.
sops.scope: Applies to all water abstraction, distribution, dyeing and finishing water use, wastewater collection, ETP operation, sludge handling, treated water reuse and effluent discharge at Unit 1 Dyeing House and Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode. It covers the EHS, Production, Quality and Administration functions involved in these activities. Head Office procurement of chemicals and equipment for the ETP is covered only where it affects effluent characteristics.

definitions.definition: Water supplied to dyeing, bleaching, washing, rinsing and finishing machines at Unit 1, excluding domestic and cooling water.
Wastewater generated from dyeing and finishing processes, including spent dye liquor, rinse water and chemical wash water, before and after treatment at Unit 2.
The Effluent Treatment Plant at Unit 2, comprising equalisation, primary and secondary treatment, sludge handling and treated water holding tanks.
Litres of fresh water consumed per kilogram of fabric or yarn processed, calculated monthly from metered inflow and production records.
Use of ETP-treated effluent for approved non-contact applications such as washing of floors or yard cleaning, under written approval from the EHS Head.
Any ETP outlet result that is above the discharge limit set in the applicable consent or the company's internal action limit for that parameter.

responsibilities: Own this SOP and ensure the ETP is operated and maintained as described.
Review daily ETP logs, approve treated water reuse and authorise any corrective action on exceedances.
Maintain the water balance and specific water consumption records.
Approve water conservation targets, reuse applications and any discharge deviation requests.
Review monthly KPI results and escalate exceedances to the Plant Head.
Ensure machine operators follow water-saving recipes, flow settings and bath-ratio standards.
Report leaks, overflows and unplanned discharges to the ETP In-charge immediately.
Provide laboratory or sampling support for effluent parameters and confirm recipe chemical changes do not affect ETP performance.
Maintain water meters, pumps, pipelines and tanks at Unit 1 and Unit 2 and arrange repairs through the work order system.
Purchase ETP chemicals and dyes only from suppliers approved by Quality and check that technical data sheets are on file.

procedure.heading: Water balance and metering
procedure.body: The ETP In-charge shall maintain a water balance for Unit 1 covering fresh water inflow, process water use, effluent generated and treated water reused or discharged. Meters at the main inlet, each process line and the ETP outlet shall be read at a fixed time each day and recorded in the water log. Any meter found to be defective shall be reported to Administration the same day.
substeps: Record daily readings at 07:00 for the previous 24 hours.
Reconcile inflow and outflow weekly and investigate any gap above 5 per cent.

procedure.heading: Water conservation at source
procedure.body: Production shall apply the approved bath-ratio, flow-rate and rinse-sequence standards for each recipe, using counter-current rinsing where the machine allows. Operators shall not run machines with partial loads below the minimum load set in the recipe card. Recipe changes that increase water use shall be approved by the EHS Head before release.

procedure.heading: Leak detection and housekeeping
procedure.body: Supervisors shall inspect process lines, valves, hoses and machine seals at the start of each shift and record findings on the shift checklist. Leaks and overflows shall be isolated and repaired by Administration through a work order, with priority given to any that discharge to drains. Hosing down of floors shall use a trigger nozzle and shall not be carried out with continuous running water.

procedure.heading: Effluent segregation and collection
procedure.body: Concentrated dye liquors, rinse waters and chemical wash waters shall be segregated into separate collection sumps at Unit 1 where practicable and conveyed to the ETP equalisation tank. No effluent shall be discharged to storm water drains. Any spill of dye, auxiliary chemical or effluent shall be contained immediately and reported to the ETP In-charge.

procedure.heading: ETP operation and monitoring
procedure.body: The ETP shall be operated in line with its operating manual, with equalisation, primary, secondary treatment and sludge handling stages run and logged each shift. Outlet samples shall be taken at the frequency set in the monitoring schedule and tested for pH, colour, COD, BOD, total suspended solids and any consent parameter specified for Unit 2. Results shall be entered in the ETP monitoring register on the day they are received.
substeps: Compare each result against the consent limit and the internal action limit.
Record the sample time, operator name and sampling point on each entry.

procedure.heading: Management of parameter exceedances
procedure.body: Where any outlet result is a parameter exceedance, the ETP In-charge shall immediately hold the discharge in the treated water tank, inform the EHS Head and Quality Lead, and take corrective action such as adjusting dosing, re-treating the batch or identifying the source. A re-sample shall be taken after corrective action and discharge shall resume only when the result is within limits. Each exceedance shall be recorded with root cause and corrective action in the non-conformity log.
substeps: Do not discharge held water until a within-limit result is confirmed.
Report any exceedance that could affect the consent to the EHS Head within 24 hours.

procedure.heading: Sludge handling and treated water reuse
procedure.body: Sludge from the ETP shall be dewatered, weighed and stored in the designated sludge area at Unit 2 before disposal through an authorised contractor. Treated water may be reused only for applications approved in writing by the EHS Head, and reuse volumes shall be recorded in the water balance. Records of sludge dispatch and reuse shall be kept as defined in the records section.

procedure.heading: Monthly review and reporting
procedure.body: The ETP In-charge shall compile the monthly water and effluent summary, including specific water consumption, reuse volume, exceedances and corrective actions. sops.title: Air Emissions Monitoring
sops.purpose: To define how Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd monitors, records and reports point-source and fugitive air emissions from the Unit 1 Dyeing House and associated boiler and thermal fluid systems at SIPCOT Perundurai, so that emissions are kept within the limits set by the applicable consent to operate and are managed in a controlled, traceable manner.
sops.scope: This procedure applies to all stacks, vents and boiler flues at Unit 1 Dyeing House, and to fugitive emissions from chemical storage and handling areas at Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, on the SIPCOT Perundurai campus. It covers stack sampling, continuous or periodic monitoring, data review, exceedance response and reporting. It does not cover effluent discharge, solid waste or occupational air quality within the workplace, which are addressed in separate procedures. Head Office, Avinashi Road, Coimbatore is outside the scope of this procedure.

definitions.definition: Emission of a air pollutant released through a defined stack, vent or flue at Unit 1 Dyeing House or a boiler house.
Unintended release of airborne substances from equipment, storage, handling or process areas that is not discharged through a defined stack or vent.
Maximum permissible concentration or mass rate of a parameter as stated in the consent to operate currently in force for the Unit, or a stricter internal limit set by the EHS Manager.
Any measured or calculated result that is above the applicable emission limit, or any reading that triggers an internal alert level defined in the monitoring plan.
Controlled document listing each emission point, parameter, method, frequency, sampling location, responsible person and applicable limit, maintained by the EHS Manager.

Documented evidence that monitoring instruments, including portable analysers and continuous monitoring systems, have been checked against traceable reference standards at the interval specified in the monitoring plan.
External laboratory engaged by Meridian Textiles to perform stack sampling and analysis, whose accreditation status is verified and recorded by the EHS Department before use.

responsibilities: Owns this procedure and maintains the monitoring plan for Unit 1 and Unit 2.
Approves the selection of external laboratories and reviews their reports.
Reviews monthly emission data, investigates exceedances and reports them to the Unit Head and management review.
Ensures the consent to operate conditions are tracked and renewal dates are calendared.
Carries out routine readings, portable analyser checks and visual inspections of stacks and boiler flues.
Records all readings in the emission log within the same shift as they are taken.
Escalates any reading above an internal alert level to the EHS Manager immediately.
Ensures dyeing and finishing batches and boiler operation follow approved parameters that minimise emissions.
Provides the EHS Executive with access to stacks and scheduled production stoppages for sampling.
Stops or reduces relevant processes when directed following an exceedance.
Ensures that monitoring instruments and reference materials are calibrated and that calibration records are retained.
Verifies that external laboratory certificates and sampling reports are filed in the controlled document system.
Arranges purchase orders for external laboratory services and maintenance of monitoring equipment at the Perundurai campus.
Maintains the statutory filing calendar with the Head Office and ensures submissions are dispatched on time.
Maintains the continuous monitoring data server, access controls and data backup for electronic emission logs.

procedure.heading: Maintain the monitoring plan
procedure.body: The EHS Manager shall prepare and maintain a monitoring plan that lists every emission point at Unit 1 and the fugitive sources at Unit 2, together with the parameters, methods, frequencies and limits. The plan shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever a process, fuel or consent condition changes.
substeps: Confirm each parameter and limit against the current consent to operate.
Record the revision number and date of approval on the plan.

procedure.heading: Carry out routine monitoring
procedure.body: The EHS Executive shall take readings and inspections at the frequencies stated in the monitoring plan. Readings shall be taken under the operating conditions normal for the relevant process, and any abnormal operating condition shall be noted alongside the result.
substeps: Check instrument calibration status before each use.
Record stack temperature, flow and fuel type where relevant.

procedure.heading: Arrange periodic stack sampling
procedure.body: Stack sampling for parameters that cannot be read on site shall be performed by an accredited laboratory at the frequency set in the monitoring plan. The EHS Manager shall approve the laboratory and the sampling scope before work begins, and the Production Manager shall schedule the required process conditions.
substeps: Verify laboratory accreditation and retain the evidence on file.
Confirm sampling ports and access platforms are safe before sampling.

procedure.heading: Record and validate data
procedure.body: All results shall be entered in the emission log or continuous monitoring system without alteration. Each entry shall be checked against the previous reading and the limit, and any missing or invalid data shall be annotated with a reason.
substeps: Do not overwrite entries; corrections are made by annotation with initials and date.
Flag any continuous monitor downtime exceeding the period stated in the monitoring plan.

procedure.heading: Respond to exceedances
procedure.body: When a reading exceeds an emission limit or alert level, the EHS Executive shall inform the EHS Manager and the Production Manager immediately. The Production Manager shall take the corrective action directed, and the EHS Manager shall decide whether the condition requires reporting to the regulator.
substeps: Record the time, parameter, process condition and immediate action taken.
Repeat the measurement once conditions are restored to confirm the outcome.

procedure.heading: Review data and report
procedure.body: The EHS Manager shall review the monthly emission data, summarise trends and exceedances, and present them at the monthly EHS review meeting. Regulatory returns shall be prepared and submitted within the deadlines stated in the consent to operate.
substeps: Coordinate with the Administration Manager for the dispatch of submissions from Head Office.
Retain copies of all submissions with proof of dispatch.

procedure.heading: Calibrate and maintain equipment
procedure.body: Portable analysers and continuous monitors shall be calibrated against traceable reference standards at the interval stated in the monitoring plan. Equipment found out of calibration shall be tagged, withdrawn and any data taken since the last valid check shall be assessed for impact.
substeps: Keep calibration certificates with the equipment register.
Record the date of the last successful check on the equipment tag.

sops.title: Workplace Safety Incident Reporting
sops.purpose: To define a consistent, timely and auditable method for reporting, recording, investigating and closing workplace safety incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that injuries are treated, causes are identified and corrective actions prevent recurrence across Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office.
sops.scope: This SOP applies to all employees, contract workers, visitors and transport or service providers present at Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse (both at SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode, Tamil Nadu) and the Head Office at Avinashi Road, Coimbatore. It covers injuries, occupational illnesses, chemical exposures and spills, fire and dye-house process hazards, near misses and unsafe conditions observed in any department.

definitions.definition: Any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, ill health, property damage, environmental release or disruption to operations.
An unplanned event that had the potential to cause harm but did not result in injury, damage or release, for example a slipped load that was caught before falling.
A physical state, arrangement or defect in the workplace, equipment or process that could lead to an incident if not corrected, such as a damaged chemical drum lid or a blocked emergency exit.
A work-related injury that prevents the affected person from attending work on the day after the injury or any subsequent scheduled shift, as recorded by the Safety Officer.
Actions taken at the time of an incident to protect people, stop further harm and secure the scene, before root cause analysis begins.
A structured review method, such as the five whys or a fishbone diagram, used to identify the underlying system or process failures behind an incident.
An action assigned to remove the identified root cause of an incident or to prevent its recurrence, with a named owner and a due date.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and maintains the incident register for all sites.
Reviews every reported incident and near miss within the timeline set in this SOP.
Leads or approves root cause analysis and verifies closure of CAPA.
Prepares the monthly EHS incident summary for management review.

responsibilities.role: Unit Head or Department Manager (Production, Quality, Administration)
responsibilities: Ensures immediate containment and first aid are provided in their area.
Completes the initial incident report with the affected employee within the stated timeline.
Implements assigned CAPA within agreed due dates and reports progress to the Safety Officer.
Records the incident in the shift log and informs the Unit Head and Safety Officer without delay.
Ensures the incident site is secured and unsafe conditions are isolated until cleared.
Confirms that witnesses are identified and available for statements.
Reports every injury, near miss and unsafe condition immediately to their supervisor, regardless of severity.
Co-operates with investigations and provides an accurate account of events.
Does not remove or alter the incident scene except to prevent further harm.
Supports the affected employee with medical referral, compensation records and return-to-work arrangements.
Maintains personnel data needed for incident records and treats health information confidentially.
Ensures that first aid stock, emergency contact lists and incident reporting forms are available at each site.
Records costs of property damage or replacement items linked to incidents when requested by the Safety Officer.

procedure.heading: Immediate response and first aid
procedure.body: The supervisor or nearest trained person must attend the casualty and provide first aid where required, and must call for medical help if the injury is serious. The area is made safe and any hazardous material is contained before anything else is done. Persons not needed for the response are moved away from the scene.
substeps: Stop the activity and isolate the energy source or chemical supply if relevant.
Record the time and location of the event in the shift log.

procedure.heading: Initial reporting
procedure.body: The person who witnessed or experienced the incident reports it to their supervisor verbally without delay. The supervisor then completes the Incident Report Form within the same shift, recording the facts only and avoiding assumptions about cause. Near misses and unsafe conditions are reported using the same form.
substeps: Form to be completed within the same shift as the event.
Photographs of the scene are taken where safe to do so.

procedure.heading: Notification to the Safety Officer
procedure.body: The Shift Supervisor notifies the Unit Head and the Safety Officer by the fastest available means, followed by submission of the completed form. Serious injuries, chemical spills, fires and any event that may require external notification are escalated immediately to the Safety Officer and the Unit Head by telephone.
substeps: Notify within two hours for injuries requiring medical treatment beyond first aid.
Escalate immediately for fatalities, hospitalisation or environmental releases.

procedure.heading: Witness statements and evidence
procedure.body: The Safety Officer or a delegated investigator collects written statements from witnesses and the affected person while memories are fresh. Equipment, records and process settings relevant to the event are preserved and labelled. Statements are signed and dated.
substeps: Preserve damaged equipment until the investigation is complete.
Record the names of all persons present at the time.

procedure.heading: Investigation and root cause analysis
procedure.body: The Safety Officer leads an investigation proportionate to the severity and potential of the event, with input from the Unit Head and a technical representative from Production or Quality where needed. The root cause analysis identifies system, process and human factors rather than attributing blame to individuals. Serious and recurring incidents require a documented analysis.
substeps: Investigation to begin within 24 hours of reporting.
Draft findings are reviewed with the Unit Head before closure.

procedure.heading: Corrective and preventive action
procedure.body: Each root cause is linked to one or more CAPA actions with a named owner, a due date and a method of verifying effectiveness. The Unit Head is accountable for implementing actions in their area, and the Safety Officer tracks them in the incident register. Actions affecting more than one site are shared across all relevant units.
substeps: Target completion for high-priority CAPA is 30 days from the investigation date.
Effectiveness is checked after a defined period, normally 90 days.

procedure.heading: Closure, communication and review
procedure.body: An incident is closed only when containment is complete, root cause is identified, CAPA is verified and the affected person's welfare requirements are recorded. Lessons learned are shared at toolbox talks and in the monthly EHS summary to management. Recurring or trend-related patterns are reviewed at the management review meeting.
substeps: Closure is signed by the Safety Officer and the Unit Head.
Trend analysis is reviewed quarterly by the Safety Officer.

sops.title: Recruitment and Onboarding
sops.purpose: To define a consistent, fair and audit-ready method for recruiting, selecting, and onboarding employees at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd so that every appointment is documented, competence-checked, and inducted to site-specific safety and quality requirements before work begins.
sops.scope: Applies to all recruitment and onboarding of permanent, fixed-term, contract and temporary staff for Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office at Avinashi Road, Coimbatore, across all departments: EHS, Production, Quality, HR, Procurement, Finance, IT and Administration. Includes internal transfers into a new role. Excludes labour supplied through third-party agencies, which is governed by the contractor management arrangements held by Procurement.

definitions.definition: A written request raised by a department head to fill a vacancy or new position, approved by the HR Manager and the relevant department head before advertising begins.
A document stating the purpose, key duties, reporting line, site location, qualifications, and safety-critical responsibilities of a role.
Any role whose holder handles chemicals, operates dyeing, finishing or ETP equipment, works at height or in confined spaces, or otherwise has a direct effect on process safety or effluent compliance.
The structured introduction to the company, site rules, emergency arrangements, and role-specific hazards delivered before an employee performs unsupervised work.
The defined initial period of employment during which performance, conduct and competence are assessed before confirmation in post.
The confidential HR record for an individual, held in hard copy or electronically under HR control, containing all onboarding documents and training records.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and maintains its currency.
Approves requisitions and job descriptions jointly with the requesting department head.
Coordinates shortlisting, interviews, offers and pre-employment checks.
Confirms that the onboarding checklist is complete before the employee starts work.

responsibilities.role: Department Head (EHS, Production, Quality, Procurement, Finance, IT, Administration)
responsibilities: Raises requisitions and defines technical and competence requirements for the role.
Sits on selection panels for technical and safety-critical roles.
Delivers role-specific on-the-job induction and confirms competence before unsupervised work.
Defines site-specific safety content for the induction of safety-critical roles at Unit 1 and Unit 2.
Verifies that safety-critical candidates receive required site safety induction and training before the work is assigned.
Maintains records of safety induction completion.
Assesses candidates against the job description using agreed, structured criteria.
Records scores and reasons for selection or rejection in the approved format.
Acts as the buddy and day-to-day point of contact for the new employee during probation.
Reviews progress at the probation checkpoints and reports concerns to HR.

procedure.heading: Raise and Approve Requisition
procedure.body: The department head completes a requisition stating the role, site, reporting line, headcount, and whether the role is safety-critical. The HR Manager reviews the request against the approved establishment and budget before advertising begins.
substeps: Confirm the role is included in the approved headcount.
Flag safety-critical roles on the requisition.

procedure.heading: Prepare Job Description
procedure.body: The job description is drafted or updated for the role and must reflect the actual duties, including any chemical handling, equipment operation, or environmental responsibilities. Both the department head and HR Manager approve it before use.

procedure.heading: Attract and Shortlist Candidates
procedure.body: Vacancies are advertised through approved channels and applications are screened against minimum qualifications and experience in the job description. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview with the time and location confirmed in writing.
substeps: Apply equal screening criteria to all applicants.
Record reasons for rejecting shortlisted candidates at this stage.

procedure.heading: Structured Interview and Selection
procedure.body: The interview panel assesses each shortlisted candidate against the same job-related criteria, including a practical or safety-awareness question for safety-critical roles. The panel records scores and a recommendation on the selection form, which is retained with the requisition file.
substeps: Include at least one technical assessor for Production, Quality and EHS roles.
Record the selection decision and rationale.

procedure.heading: Pre-Employment Checks and Offer
procedure.body: Before an offer is confirmed, HR verifies identity, qualifications, and previous employment references, and obtains any medical fitness declaration required for the role. A written offer stating the terms, start date, site, and probation period is then issued and signed by the candidate.
substeps: Obtain medical fitness confirmation for safety-critical roles.
Verify original qualifications against the candidate's documents.

procedure.heading: Pre-Joining Preparation and Personnel File
procedure.body: A Personnel File is opened and the onboarding checklist is issued to the relevant departments before the start date. IT provisions accounts, Administration issues access cards and personal protective equipment as applicable, and HR confirms that all signed documents are on file.
substeps: Issue PPE sizing and access requests at least three working days before start date.
Confirm policy acknowledgements are on file.

procedure.heading: Induction and Competence Sign-Off
procedure.body: On the first day, the employee attends a general induction covering company policies, emergency arrangements and the relevant site. Safety-critical employees complete the site safety induction and role-specific training before they undertake any task, and the line manager confirms competence before unsupervised work is allowed.
procedure.responsible: HR Manager / EHS Manager / Department Head
substeps: Deliver site induction specific to Unit 1, Unit 2 or Head Office.
Record competence sign-off for each safety-critical task.
Hold the employee on supervised duties until sign-off is recorded.

procedure.heading: Probation Review and Confirmation
procedure.body: Performance, conduct and competence are reviewed at defined checkpoints during the probation period. The line manager and HR jointly decide whether to confirm the employee, extend probation, or end the appointment, and record the outcome in the Personnel File.
substeps: Hold a formal review at the midpoint and at the end of probation.
Record any extension with its reason and new end date.

sops.title: Employee Performance Evaluation
sops.purpose: To define a consistent, fair and documented process for evaluating the performance of all employees at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that performance is measured against agreed objectives, development needs are identified, and outcomes inform pay, promotion and training decisions across Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office.
sops.scope: This procedure applies to all permanent, probationary and fixed-term employees of Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd at Unit 1 Dyeing House (SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode), Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse (same campus), and the Head Office (Avinashi Road, Coimbatore), across the EHS, Production, Quality, HR, Procurement, Finance, IT and Administration departments. It does not cover contract labour supplied through third-party agencies, whose performance is managed under their service agreements.

definitions.definition: A formal, periodic review in which an employee's results, behaviours and development are assessed against agreed objectives and role expectations.
The defined review period, comprising a mid-year review and an annual year-end review, during which objectives are set, monitored and assessed.
A specific, measurable and time-bound goal agreed between the employee and reviewer at the start of an evaluation cycle, linked to departmental plans.
The line manager or supervisor who holds direct responsibility for the employee's day-to-day work and who conducts the evaluation.
The overall outcome grade assigned at year-end on the company's five-point scale, derived from objective achievement and competency assessment.
A documented set of training, coaching and experience actions agreed to address identified skill gaps or support career progression.
A review group convened by the HR Manager, with department heads, to check consistency of ratings across departments and sites before they are finalised.

responsibilities: Owns, maintains and revises this SOP and the associated evaluation forms.
Schedules evaluation cycles and communicates timelines to all departments and sites.
Chairs the Calibration Panel and approves final ratings.
Maintains evaluation records and reports KPIs to the management review.

responsibilities.role: Department Heads (EHS, Production, Quality, Procurement, Finance, IT, Administration)
responsibilities: Ensure every employee in their department has a named Reviewer and agreed objectives.
Participate in calibration to ensure consistent ratings across departments.
Review and countersign completed evaluations for their teams.
Set objectives with employees at the start of each cycle and record them on the evaluation form.
Conduct mid-year and year-end review meetings and document evidence of performance.
Agree development plans and ensure follow-up actions are tracked.
Prepare a self-assessment before each review meeting.
Raise concerns about objectives or ratings through the grievance route.
Complete agreed development actions within the agreed timescales.
Applies approved ratings to variable pay and increment calculations.
Confirms that pay outcomes match the ratings recorded by HR.
Maintains the HR information system or secure electronic form used for evaluation records, including access control and backup.

procedure.heading: Cycle planning
procedure.body: The HR Manager issues the evaluation calendar at least four weeks before each cycle opens, specifying the mid-year and year-end review windows for all three locations. The calendar is circulated to department heads and posted on the HR notice board at each site.
substeps: Confirm the review windows for Unit 1, Unit 2 and Head Office.
Issue the calendar and evaluation forms to all Reviewers.

procedure.heading: Objective setting
procedure.body: Each Reviewer meets the employee within the first three weeks of the cycle to agree between three and five objectives, each linked to a departmental goal. Objectives are recorded on the evaluation form and signed by both parties.
substeps: Ensure objectives are specific, measurable and time-bound.
Record any role-specific competencies to be assessed.

procedure.heading: Ongoing monitoring
procedure.body: Reviewers record evidence of performance throughout the cycle, including output and quality data, safety observations and feedback received. Where performance falls below expectation, the Reviewer raises the matter promptly in a private discussion and agrees support actions.

procedure.heading: Employee self-assessment
procedure.body: The employee completes a self-assessment against each objective and competency at least five working days before the review meeting. The self-assessment is submitted to the Reviewer and forms part of the discussion.

procedure.heading: Review meeting
procedure.body: The Reviewer conducts a documented meeting, comparing evidence with the agreed objectives and discussing the employee's self-assessment. Both parties record agreed comments, and the employee is given the opportunity to add their own remarks before the form is signed.
substeps: Hold the meeting in private and allow sufficient time for discussion.
Record any disagreement in the employee's comments section.

procedure.heading: Calibration and approval
procedure.body: Department heads check proposed ratings for consistency at the Calibration Panel, which the HR Manager chairs. The panel may adjust ratings where evidence does not support the proposed grade, and the reason for any change is recorded.
substeps: Compare rating distributions across departments and sites.
Record the reason for every adjusted rating.

procedure.heading: Development planning and pay linkage
procedure.body: Reviewers agree a development plan with each employee addressing identified gaps, and HR records it against the employee's file. Approved ratings are passed to Finance for application to pay and increments, and the outcome is communicated to the employee in writing.
substeps: Log training actions in the training plan.
Confirm pay outcomes with Finance before the cycle closes.

procedure.heading: Records and appeals
procedure.body: Signed evaluation forms are filed in the employee's personnel record within ten working days of final approval. An employee who disagrees with a rating may appeal in writing to the HR Manager within ten working days, and the appeal is reviewed by a manager not involved in the original rating.
substeps: Retain records in line with the retention schedule in this manual.
Log and close all appeals with a written outcome.

sops.title: Grievance Handling
sops.purpose: To establish a fair, confidential and timely process for receiving, recording, investigating and resolving grievances raised by employees, workers and contract labour at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that concerns are addressed without reprisal and lessons are fed back into HR and operational practice.
sops.scope: Applies to all permanent employees, trainees, contract labour and visiting workers at Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office, Avinashi Road, Coimbatore. Covers individual and collective grievances on terms of employment, working conditions, pay, shift allocation, harassment, discrimination, health and safety concerns raised as personal grievances, and conduct of supervisors. Matters of statutory compliance audits and whistleblowing on fraud are handled under their own procedures but must be referred to HR where they involve a worker's personal complaint.

definitions.definition: Any concern, complaint or dissatisfaction raised by an individual or group about their employment, working conditions, treatment or workplace relationships, whether raised verbally or in writing.
The employee, worker or contract labourer who raises a grievance under this SOP.
The person or department whose action, decision or omission is the subject of a grievance.
The HR executive nominated by the HR Manager to receive, log and coordinate grievances at the relevant site.
A manager independent of the grievance subject, appointed by the HR Manager to establish facts and recommend a resolution.
Referral of an unresolved grievance to the next level of management or to the HR Manager, as set out in this SOP.
The controlled log, held by HR, in which every grievance is recorded with its date, category, status, owner and closure date.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and ensures it is reviewed and approved as set out in the review section.
Appoints Investigating Officers and approves final outcomes of grievances that are escalated.
Reviews the Grievance Register monthly and reports trends to site leadership.
Receives, logs and acknowledges grievances at Unit 1, Unit 2 and Head Office.
Maintains confidentiality and keeps the complainant informed of progress.
Tracks timelines and prompts escalation where closure targets are at risk.
Cooperate with investigations and provide records of shift, task and performance data when requested.
Take immediate interim measures to protect the complainant where safety or harassment is alleged.
Implement agreed corrective actions within the agreed timeframe.
Advises on grievances with health and safety content and ensures they are linked to the incident reporting process where relevant.
Confirms that effluent treatment and chemical handling concerns raised as grievances are assessed for safety impact.
Conducts impartial fact-finding, interviews relevant parties and documents evidence.
Submits a written findings report with recommended outcome within the timeline set in this SOP.
Ensure workers are aware of the grievance route and that no reprisal occurs.
Review repeated or systemic grievances and address root causes in their departments.

procedure.heading: Raising a grievance
procedure.body: Any worker may raise a grievance verbally or in writing with a supervisor, the HR Executive at the site, or through the grievance box located at each unit. Supervisors receiving a grievance must refer it to the Grievance Officer within one working day and must not attempt to resolve it informally without recording it.
substeps: Grievance forms are available in English and Tamil at each unit gate and HR office.
Anonymous submissions are accepted and logged, though their investigation may be limited.

procedure.heading: Logging and acknowledgement
procedure.body: The Grievance Officer records each grievance in the Grievance Register, assigns a reference number and classifies it by category and urgency. Written acknowledgement is provided to the complainant within two working days, confirming the reference number and the expected timeline.
substeps: Urgent matters involving safety, harassment or threats are flagged for same-day review by the HR Manager.

procedure.heading: Interim protection
procedure.body: Where a grievance alleges harassment, discrimination, unsafe conditions or retaliation, the HR Manager determines within one working day whether interim measures are required, such as temporary change of shift, reporting line or work area. Interim measures must not disadvantage the complainant in pay or status.

procedure.heading: Assessment and appointment of investigator
procedure.body: The Grievance Officer assesses whether the grievance can be resolved informally by the line manager within five working days. Where it cannot, the HR Manager appoints an Investigating Officer who has no direct reporting connection to the complainant or respondent.
substeps: Informal resolution is recorded in the register with the agreed outcome and the complainant's confirmation.

procedure.heading: Investigation
procedure.body: The Investigating Officer interviews the complainant, respondent and relevant witnesses, reviews attendance, shift, pay and other relevant records, and documents all evidence. Respondents are given the right to respond to the allegations in writing before findings are made. The investigation should be completed within fifteen working days of appointment, or the HR Manager must approve and record an extension with reasons.
substeps: Interview notes are signed by the interviewee and held confidentially by HR.
Companion or union representation is permitted where the complainant or respondent requests it under company policy.

procedure.heading: Decision and communication of outcome
procedure.body: The Investigating Officer submits a findings report to the HR Manager, who decides on the outcome and any corrective or disciplinary action. The complainant receives a written response explaining the outcome, reasons and any action taken, without disclosing confidential information about other individuals.

procedure.heading: Appeal and escalation
procedure.body: A complainant who is dissatisfied with the outcome may submit a written appeal to the Head of Administration within ten working days of receiving the outcome. The appeal is reviewed by a manager not previously involved, and a final decision is communicated in writing within fifteen working days.
substeps: Appeals must state the grounds for disagreement with the outcome or the process followed.

procedure.heading: Closure, follow-up and learning
procedure.body: The Grievance Officer closes the entry in the Grievance Register only after the agreed corrective actions are verified as implemented. The HR Manager reviews closed cases monthly for recurring themes and reports systemic issues to site leadership for preventive action.
substeps: Follow-up with the complainant is held at 30 and 90 days after closure to confirm no reprisal has occurred.

sops.title: Approval of Sensitive Transactions
sops.purpose: To define how sensitive financial transactions at Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd are identified, authorised, executed and recorded, so that payments, bank changes, journal adjustments and other high-risk entries receive independent approval before they are processed across Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office at Avinashi Road, Coimbatore.
sops.scope: This SOP applies to all transactions classed as sensitive under this procedure that are initiated, approved or posted by Finance, Procurement, Production, Administration and HR personnel at all three sites. It covers vendor master changes, bank detail changes, payments above the delegated limits, manual journal entries, write-offs, credit note issues outside standard terms, payroll master changes and any transaction the CFO designates as sensitive. It does not cover routine, system-generated transactions within approved limits.

definitions.definition: A financial transaction or master data change that carries elevated risk of error or misappropriation, as listed in the Sensitive Transaction Register maintained by Finance, and requiring approval under this SOP before processing.
The authorised employee who raises a sensitive transaction request, supplies supporting documents and confirms its business purpose.

A person who approves a sensitive transaction and who is not the initiator, does not hold the same request in another workflow step, and holds delegated authority for the value and type of transaction.
The approved schedule, issued by the CFO, setting out monetary limits and transaction types each role may approve.
The separation of initiation, approval, execution and recording of a transaction so that no single person controls all stages.
Confirmation of a payee or bank detail change through a call-back to a contact already held on the vendor master, independent of details supplied in the request.
The register, maintained in the finance system or as a controlled spreadsheet, recording each sensitive transaction, its approvers, dates and outcome.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and the Sensitive Transaction Register.
Issues and revises the Delegation of Authority Matrix.
Approves transactions above the highest delegated limit and reviews the Approval Log monthly.
Checks completeness of requests and supporting documents before routing for approval.
Performs dual verification for bank and vendor changes.
Maintains the Approval Log and prepares monthly exception reports for the CFO.
Raise sensitive transaction requests with accurate business justification and supporting documents.
Do not approve their own requests or split transactions to avoid limits.
Review each request against the Delegation of Authority Matrix and supporting evidence.
Approve, reject or return requests with a recorded reason within two working days.
Configures system workflow so that initiators cannot approve their own requests.
Restricts edit rights on vendor and bank master data to authorised Finance staff and maintains access logs.
Samples approved transactions each quarter to test compliance with this SOP.
Reports exceptions to the CFO and the Audit Committee where one exists.

procedure.heading: Identification of sensitive transactions
procedure.body: Finance identifies each transaction type that meets the sensitive criteria and records it in the Sensitive Transaction Register. The register is reviewed by the CFO every six months and whenever a new transaction type or site process is introduced.
substeps: Confirm the transaction type against the register before submission.
Record any new type with its approval threshold.

procedure.heading: Raising the request
procedure.body: The initiator completes the Sensitive Transaction Request form, stating the purpose, amount, payee or account affected and supporting documents such as invoices, contracts or bank confirmation letters. The request must be submitted through the finance workflow or the controlled request form at the initiating site. Incomplete requests are not accepted for review.
substeps: Attach all supporting documents before submission.
Do not split a transaction to avoid a delegated limit.

procedure.heading: Completeness check
procedure.body: The Finance Manager checks that the request is complete, that the transaction type is correctly classified and that the initiator is authorised for that type. Requests failing the check are returned to the initiator with the reason recorded in the Approval Log. Each request is checked within one working day of receipt.

procedure.heading: Dual verification of payee or bank changes
procedure.body: For any new or changed vendor bank detail, the Finance Manager contacts the vendor using a telephone number already held on the approved vendor master, not one supplied in the request. The call-back outcome, the name of the person contacted and the date are recorded on the request before approval. Changes that cannot be verified are rejected.
substeps: Use only contact details held before the change request was received.
Record the call-back outcome on the request form.

procedure.heading: Independent approval
procedure.body: The request is routed to an Independent Approver whose delegated authority covers the amount and type. Approval is recorded electronically or on the signed form. Where the amount exceeds the highest delegated limit, the CFO approves. Approvers must not approve requests they initiated or that they prepared for posting.
substeps: Confirm the approver is not the initiator or the preparer.
Return or reject the request with a written reason where evidence is inadequate.

procedure.heading: Execution and posting
procedure.body: Only after approval is recorded may the transaction be executed or posted. The person executing the payment or journal must be different from the approver. The executed reference, date and amount are entered against the approval record so that the two can be matched.
substeps: Compare executed amount and payee with the approved request before release.
Record the bank or journal reference on the Approval Log.

procedure.heading: Monitoring and exception reporting
procedure.body: The Finance Manager reviews the Approval Log monthly to identify approvals outside authority, late approvals, repeated returns and transactions without matching execution records. Exceptions are reported to the CFO with proposed corrective action. Access rights found to be excessive are referred to IT for correction.
substeps: Investigate any approval outside delegated authority within five working days.
Confirm closure of each exception in the next monthly report.

procedure.heading: Internal audit review
procedure.body: Internal Audit or a nominated reviewer samples approved sensitive transactions each quarter across all three sites and checks the request, verification evidence, approval and execution match. Findings are reported to the CFO and tracked to closure. Results inform the next revision of this SOP.

Vendor and bank change requests verified by call-back before approval

Training attendance is recorded by HR and retained with training records. IT provides training on the workflow system to users with approval rights.
