sops.title: Confidential Data Breach Response
sops.purpose: To define a controlled, timely and auditable response to any actual or suspected breach of confidential data held by Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, so that incidents are contained, assessed, reported internally and externally where required, and used to strengthen controls across Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office at Avinashi Road, Coimbatore.
sops.scope: This SOP applies to all confidential data held in any form by Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, including customer and export buyer specifications, costing and pricing data, supplier and procurement records, employee and HR personal data, production recipes and formulations, and financial information. It applies to all employees, contractors and third-party service providers with access to company systems or information at all three sites, and to all IT systems, email, shared drives, mobile devices and paper records.

definitions.definition: Any information held by the company that is not intended for public disclosure, including buyer specifications, dye recipes, pricing, employee personal data and financial records.
A security incident that leads to accidental or unlawful loss, destruction, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to confidential data, whether in electronic or paper form.
A situation reported or observed where there are reasonable grounds to believe a data breach may have occurred, pending confirmation by the IT Manager.
The standing group comprising the IT Manager, EHS representative, HR representative, Quality representative and Finance representative, convened to manage a confirmed or suspected breach.
Actions taken to stop a breach from spreading or continuing, such as disabling compromised accounts, isolating devices or recalling misdirected documents.
The controlled register in which every reported breach, suspected breach and near miss is recorded with its timeline, actions and closure details.

responsibilities: Owns this SOP and chairs the Incident Response Team.
Confirms or rejects suspected breaches and directs technical containment and forensic review.
Maintains the incident log and ensures records are retained as specified.
Report any actual or suspected breach immediately to the IT helpdesk or IT Manager, without attempting to investigate independently.
Do not delete, alter or forward affected data or evidence unless instructed by the IT Manager.
Advises on breaches involving employee personal data and manages staff-related communications.
Ensures disciplinary matters arising from a breach are handled under company procedure.
Represents the Incident Response Team for physical records and site-based incidents across Unit 1 and Unit 2.
Supports the investigation where a breach involves unauthorised access to controlled premises or storage areas.
Assess financial and commercial impact of a breach, including exposure of pricing or supplier terms.
Notify affected commercial partners where contractual confidentiality clauses require it, as approved by the Managing Director.
Manages physical security controls and retrieval of misdirected paper records at Head Office and the Unit 2 Warehouse.
Supports the IT Manager in confirming access logs for physical areas.

procedure.heading: Identify and report
procedure.body: Any person who discovers or suspects a breach of confidential data must report it immediately to the IT helpdesk or the IT Manager, by phone or email, and note the time of discovery. The report should describe what data is involved, where it was found and who may be affected. Reports must be made within one hour of discovery, including outside normal working hours via the on-call IT contact.
procedure.responsible: Employee or contractor who discovers the breach
substeps: State the site, system or document involved.
Preserve the device or record as found; do not switch off devices unless instructed.

procedure.heading: Log and triage
procedure.body: The IT Manager records the report in the incident log with a unique reference number, date, time and reporter details. The IT Manager then classifies the event as a confirmed breach, a suspected breach or a non-incident within four working hours. Classification determines the urgency and the members of the Incident Response Team to be convened.
substeps: Assign a severity rating based on data sensitivity and number of individuals affected.
Close non-incidents with a documented reason and record them as near misses where relevant.

procedure.heading: Contain
procedure.body: The IT Manager directs immediate containment to prevent further loss, including suspending affected user accounts, revoking shared links, isolating compromised devices and blocking outbound transfers. Physical containment, such as securing paper records or locking affected areas, is directed through the Administration Manager and EHS Manager. Containment actions must be completed as soon as practicable and no later than four hours after classification.
procedure.responsible: IT Manager with Administration Manager and EHS Manager
substeps: Retrieve or request deletion of misdirected emails or files from unintended recipients, obtaining written confirmation.
Change credentials for any accounts or systems that may have been compromised.

procedure.heading: Convene the Incident Response Team and investigate
procedure.body: The IT Manager convenes the Incident Response Team, which meets within 24 hours for severe incidents and within three working days for minor incidents. The team establishes what data was affected, how the breach occurred, the time window involved and the number and category of data subjects or commercial partners potentially impacted. Evidence is preserved, including system logs, access records and affected documents, under chain-of-custody controls.
procedure.responsible: IT Manager (chair) with Incident Response Team
substeps: Obtain relevant access and audit logs from system administrators.
Record all findings in the incident log against the reference number.

procedure.heading: Assess impact and decide on notifications
procedure.body: The Incident Response Team assesses the likely harm to individuals, customers, suppliers and the company, taking account of the nature and sensitivity of the data. The Managing Director decides whether affected individuals, export buyers or other third parties must be notified, and whether any regulatory notification is required under applicable law. The legal basis and decision for each notification are documented in the incident log.
procedure.responsible: IT Manager, HR Manager, Finance Manager and Managing Director
substeps: Confirm contractual confidentiality obligations to buyers and suppliers before any notification is issued.
Use only approved wording for external communications, reviewed by the Managing Director.

procedure.heading: Recover and remediate
procedure.body: Once containment is confirmed, the IT Manager oversees restoration of affected systems and data from verified backups, and confirms that the vulnerability used has been closed. Corrective actions, such as access reviews, configuration changes, retraining or updated controls, are assigned with named owners and target dates. Restoration and corrective actions are verified before the incident is closed.
procedure.responsible: IT Manager with relevant department heads
substeps: Confirm that restored data has integrity and has been checked against the last known good state.
Assign corrective actions with owner and due date in the incident log.

procedure.heading: Review and close
procedure.body: The IT Manager prepares a written incident report summarising the cause, timeline, impact, actions taken and lessons learned, and presents it to the Managing Director and the Incident Response Team. The incident is formally closed only when all corrective actions are verified and notifications are complete. Lessons learned are fed into the risk register and training plan.
substeps: Record closure date and approver in the incident log.
Share relevant lessons with all three sites through departmental briefings.

procedure.heading: Monitor and report KPIs
procedure.body: The IT Manager reviews breach metrics monthly and reports trends to the Managing Director, including response times and open corrective actions. Any repeated incident category triggers a focused review of the relevant control. Results are used to revise this SOP at the scheduled review.
substeps: Compile KPI data from the incident log at the end of each month.
Escalate overdue corrective actions to the responsible department head.

sops.training: All employees and contractors at Unit 1, Unit 2 and Head Office receive induction training on identifying and reporting data breaches before accessing company systems. Incident Response Team members complete role-specific training on containment, evidence preservation and notification decisions annually. Refresher awareness briefings are delivered at least annually and after any significant incident, with attendance recorded by the HR department.

sops.title: Supplier ESG Due Diligence
sops.purpose: To define how Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd assesses, approves, monitors and re-assesses environmental, social and governance (ESG) risk in its suppliers of dyes, chemicals, auxiliaries, yarn, greige fabric, packaging and services, so that supply to export brands is sourced only from suppliers whose risk is understood, documented and within the company's accepted limits.
sops.scope: This procedure applies to all new and existing suppliers of materials and services to Unit 1 Dyeing House, Unit 2 Effluent Treatment Plant and Warehouse, and the Head Office, Avinashi Road, Coimbatore, at SIPCOT Perundurai, Erode, and Head Office. It covers chemical and dye suppliers, raw cotton yarn and greige fabric suppliers, subcontracted finishing or logistics providers, and ETP and waste contractors. It is owned by the Procurement Head within the Procurement department and is read with the wider Meridian manual, MTPL/SOP/01, Revision 01.

definitions.definition: Any external organisation that supplies goods or services to Meridian Textiles Pvt Ltd, including direct and sub-tier suppliers where known.
The documented process of identifying, assessing and recording environmental, social and governance risks associated with a supplier before and during the business relationship.
A supplier whose failure or non-compliance would materially affect production, effluent compliance, product safety or delivery to export brands, as classified by the Procurement Head with EHS input.

Any chemical, dye or auxiliary that is prohibited or restricted under the company's Restricted Substances List or under a customer's requirement, and which must not be supplied to or used at Meridian sites without written approval.
The score allocated to a supplier, classed as Low, Medium or High, derived from the completed assessment questionnaire, document review and any site verification.
A written plan agreed with a supplier that sets out the non-conformity, the required corrective action, the responsible person and the agreed completion date.
The controlled register of suppliers cleared for use, showing each supplier's ESG Risk Rating, approval status and next review date.

responsibilities: Owns this procedure and the Approved Supplier List.
Classifies Critical Suppliers and approves or rejects supplier onboarding.
Issues and tracks Corrective Action Plans and decides on suspension or removal of suppliers.
Reviews environmental and health and safety evidence, including effluent, emissions, chemical handling and waste contractor credentials.
Carries out or directs site verification visits for High-risk and dyeing-related suppliers.
Advises on Restricted Substance status of chemicals and dyes.
Reviews labour practice evidence, including working hours, wages, freedom of association and child and forced labour controls.
Advises on grievance handling and supplier workforce concerns raised through company channels.
Confirms that product safety and customer restricted substance requirements are reflected in supplier documentation.
Approves or rejects materials for production use where a Restricted Substance concern is raised.
Confirms supplier legal entity, banking and governance details and flags conflicts of interest or payment irregularities.
Holds supplier master data controls to prevent onboarding without completed due diligence.
Maintains the supplier questionnaire platform and access controls, and the retention of electronic supplier records.

procedure.heading: Supplier Identification and Categorisation
procedure.body: The requesting department raises a supplier onboarding request on the company's approved form, stating the goods or services, the site of use and the expected annual value. The Procurement Head classifies the supplier as Critical or standard and records the classification in the ASL.
substeps: Confirm whether the supplier will handle chemicals, dyes, effluent or wastes.
Record any known sub-tier suppliers for high-risk inputs.

procedure.heading: Issue of ESG Questionnaire
procedure.body: The Procurement team issues the supplier ESG self-assessment questionnaire covering environment, labour, health and safety, ethics, governance and supply chain transparency. The supplier must return the completed questionnaire with supporting documents within the period stated in the request.
substeps: Use the current questionnaire version held on the IT-controlled platform.
Record the date of issue and the response deadline in the supplier file.

procedure.heading: Document Review and Risk Scoring
procedure.body: Procurement reviews the returned questionnaire and evidence against the company's ESG criteria. EHS, HR and Quality review their respective sections, and each scores the supplier, after which the Procurement Head allocates an overall ESG Risk Rating of Low, Medium or High.
substeps: Check Restricted Substance declarations against the current list and customer requirements.
Check effluent and waste contractor licences and disposal records where applicable.

procedure.heading: Site Verification
procedure.body: Where a supplier is rated High, is a Critical Supplier handling dyeing chemicals, or has provided incomplete evidence, EHS or Procurement arranges a site verification visit or an agreed remote review. The visit findings are recorded on the verification checklist and shared with the supplier.
substeps: Observe chemical storage, labelling and effluent discharge points where relevant.
Interview workers on working hours, wages and grievance access, where practicable.

procedure.heading: Approval Decision and Corrective Action
procedure.body: The Procurement Head decides whether to approve, approve with conditions or reject the supplier based on the risk rating and verification findings. Any non-conformity must be recorded with a Corrective Action Plan agreed with the supplier before first order or within an agreed period for conditional approval.
substeps: Reject suppliers that refuse to disclose Restricted Substance data or that hold unresolved serious non-compliance.
Record conditional approvals with a re-review date no later than six months ahead.

procedure.heading: Contractual Commitments
procedure.body: Approved suppliers must sign the company's supplier code of conduct and accept ESG clauses covering restricted substances, effluent and waste compliance, labour standards and audit rights. No purchase order is released to a supplier without a signed code and an active ASL entry.
substeps: Confirm that the Finance Head has completed supplier master data checks before the first payment.
Store the signed code in the supplier file.

procedure.heading: Ongoing Monitoring and Re-assessment
procedure.body: Approved suppliers are monitored through performance reviews, incident reports, complaints and periodic re-assessment. High-risk suppliers are re-assessed annually, Medium-risk suppliers every two years, and Low-risk suppliers every three years, or sooner after any material incident or change in supply.
substeps: Trigger an immediate re-assessment after any effluent exceedance, chemical incident or customer complaint linked to the supplier.
Suspend or remove suppliers from the ASL where a CAP is not met by the agreed date.
